A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AIDD and contain readable methods, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched reliably across the revisions.

before.justification: v3 reports original MusicNet and MAESTRO inpainting experiments and training-strategy ablations in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v4 retains original inpainting experiments and adds listening-test, tokenizer, latency and diagnostic results, including in its appendices.

M1.justification: The core DiT/DWDSE framework, derivative loss and span-masking procedure remain unchanged. v4 adds an evaluated UniCodec substitution for WavTokenizer and changes inference boundary crossfading from 6 to 10 ms (Sections 4.1, 5.2 and 7), constituting limited component and inference changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MusicNet classical music with four 150–300 ms gaps and MAESTRO piano recordings with single 375/750 ms gaps. The added listening and codec/masking checks use the same data and concern evaluation metrics or preprocessing controls. Single- and multiple-gap coverage already existed in v3.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in MusicNet Table 1 and MAESTRO Table 2 are unchanged. v4 additionally evaluates CQT-Diff+ alongside GACELA in the MAESTRO listening comparison (Table 3) and includes CQT-Diff+ in the new latency comparison (Table 6); its earlier reported comparison was on MusicNet.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 revises training segments from 1024 tokens, approximately 13.6 seconds, to 300 tokens, approximately 4 seconds, and crossfading from 6 to 10 ms. v4 adds randomized, anonymized 1–5 MOS evaluation using five clips per gap duration per method plus five original references, alongside latency and diagnostic protocols. These substantially expand evaluation design; the PDFs do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The original span/derivative hyperparameter ablation is retained as v4 Table 4. New analyses test tokenizer choice (Table 5), encoding/decoding and gap-stitching losses (Appendix A, Table 7), masking before versus after tokenization (Appendix C, Table 9), and computational cost (Section 8, Table 6). These substantially broaden the investigation of components and methodological assumptions.

E5.justification: Both versions average ten stochastic reconstructions per MusicNet segment and use ± reporting in existing ODG and ablation tables. v4 applies the same undefined ± convention to MOS but adds no specified seed protocol, repeated-run increase, confidence intervals or significance tests. Additional rows and changed numerical spreads are result changes.

E6.justification: MusicNet Table 1 and the matched training-ablation values remain unchanged. MAESTRO AIDD ODG changes from -2.370±0.705 to -2.303±0.692 at 375 ms and from -2.959±0.604 to -2.596±1.300 at 750 ms (Table 2); changed reported settings prevent assuming a same-setting gain. v4 adds MOS results, including 3.64 for AIDD versus 3.51 for both GACELA and CQT-Diff+, plus tokenizer, latency and diagnostic results in Tables 5–7 and 9.

T1.justification: The forward/reverse diffusion equations, DWDSE objective, temporal-derivative definitions, span-length schedule and LSD formula are mathematically unchanged. The new explanation that span masking can produce multiple disjoint spans clarifies the existing procedure. No new theorem, proof or formal derivation appears.

C1.justification: The central novelty, long-gap restoration and span/derivative contributions remain. The introduction extends the performance contribution to explicitly claim consistent subjective as well as objective evaluation results. Its single/multiple-gap wording clarifies coverage already evaluated in v3.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive limitations concerning tokenizer fidelity, the 24 kHz output restriction, comparison biases and training–inference masking mismatch (Section 8). It introduces a vocabulary-size explanation for UniCodec's weaker results and interprets appendix diagnostics as showing tokenization-dominated degradation and little masking-order effect. It also removes v3's interpretation that success on a reduced MAESTRO subset demonstrates data efficiency.

D1.justification: v4 expands the hyperparameter documentation with vocabulary sizes, EMA, gradient accumulation, temperature, noise schedule and Euler sampling, and adds model/codec sizes. It supplies GitHub and Hugging Face access links where v3 promised public code after acceptance. Conversely, the MAESTRO training/test subset disclosure and offer to supply its file list disappear; v4 does not establish whether full splits were subsequently used.

R1.justification: v4 adds Jiang et al. (2025), UniCodec, and discusses it as an alternative to WavTokenizer. The existing related-work account and claimed novelty remain largely unchanged. The widespread switch from numbered to author-year citations is formatting rather than expanded research positioning.

P1.justification: Most introductory, related-work and method prose is retained. v4 condenses dataset/results passages and substantially shortens the conclusion, inserts a Discussion section, reorganizes appendices, and updates affiliations, citation style and selected explanations. Editing of the existing narrative remains localized.

P2.justification: v4 adds tables for MOS, tokenizer comparison, latency, information loss and masking order (Tables 3, 5, 6, 7 and 9), and substantially expands the earlier hyperparameter table as Table 8. Existing displays are repositioned or resized. Figure 1 retains the identical graphic but changes size, placement and caption wording. The evidence displays are substantially expanded.

improvement.justification: v4 improves scrutiny of tokenizer dependence and masking mismatch, adds measured latency and useful implementation details, and acknowledges concrete bandwidth and comparison limitations absent from v3. These benefits are limited by the listening study's missing participant count and undefined uncertainty despite a small MOS lead (3.64 versus 3.51), and by removal of the MAESTRO subset disclosure while settings and scores change.
